item.content:encoded:
Three days of calm in Kyiv. Day 1658 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Russian forces have finally withdrawn from the areas west of the Netryus River and, according to some sources, also from positions between it and the Zherebets River. Confirmation of this information will mean that the breach in Ukrainian defences has been closed, thereby ending the encirclement of Lyman and Sloviansk from the north, and that at least five towns and at least part of Lyman have returned to the control of the defenders (the Russians are still reported to be holding the eastern outskirts of the city). The reason for Russia’s decision to abandon the breach must be seen as the Ukrainians’ effective disruption of Russian logistics, particularly river crossings, as well as a lack of forces to extend the encirclement. The Russians had found themselves in a similar situation on two previous occasions – in November 2022, when they withdrew from the right-bank part of Kherson Oblast, and in December 2025, when they were driven out of the western part of Kupiansk in Kharkiv Oblast.

The Russians have made significant advances to the south and east of the Sloviansk-Kramatorsk conurbation. They have deepened their encirclement of Dobropillia, which is currently the scene of fighting. Their sabotage and reconnaissance groups (SRGs) have reached Bilozerka, situated north of that town. item.title: [19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland] A bridge too far? Ukraine’s operation to isolate Crimea
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
A bridge too far? Ukraine’s operation to isolate Crimea

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Over the past three months, Ukraine has intensified its attacks on the Russian army’s operational rear on Crimea. The targets have included logistics hubs, road, rail and maritime infrastructure, troop concentrations, air defence systems, ammunition depots and command posts. The operation aims to cut the peninsula off from military reinforcements and fuel supplies, while also damaging energy infrastructure and transport links used to supply the civilian population. The scale of the disruption prompted the occupation authorities on Crimea to declare a state of emergency in late June, which remains in force. Medium-range unmanned aerial vehicles have played a particularly important role in these attacks.

Despite the substantial damage inflicted by Ukrainian strikes, they have so far had no significant impact on the pace of the Russian army’s advance at the front. Russian forces retain the initiative and continue to exert pressure along most sections of Ukraine’s defensive line, including in the southern sector. Russian troops in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts are supplied largely through Crimea. A possible destruction of the Crimean Bridge could alter the situation on the peninsula. However, Ukraine’s ability to achieve this objective is constrained by the limited technical capabilities of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) and the potential consequences of such an operation.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Amendment to China’s National Defence Mobilisation Law

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

On 31 August, Xi Jinping promulgated an amendment to the 2010 National Defence Mobilisation Law of the People’s Republic of China (中华人民共和国国防动员法), which will enter into force on 1 October this year. The amendment does not fundamentally overhaul China’s mobilisation system, but significantly expands the state’s capacity to rapidly mobilise all types of resources, including technological and digital assets. It also strengthens the direct leadership role of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and Xi Jinping himself, effectively removing state institutions from the decision-making process. It further deepens civil-military fusion, tightens control over supply chains and the reserve system and establishes a mechanism to control data, technology and economic resources. There are currently no grounds to regard these legislative changes as part of Beijing’s planning for any specific offensive action in the near term. However, they are consistent with a long-term policy of systematically preparing China for a potential conflict with the United States.

For the first time, the law defines mobilisation and states that its purpose is ‘to ensure a rapid transition between peace and war’. The amended law links mobilisation with economic development and the emergency response system, with provisions covering strategic reserves, transport, healthcare and cybersecurity.
